messages:
maya: Heads-up — ran a shard-sizing + allocator sweep on the dedicated pools and hit a cluster of OOMs. Pattern: prefix cache shard_count=32 + workspace_limit=1.2GB. Profiling suggests heavy fragmentation and lots of fallback small allocs. Sharing initial notes, looking for quick mitigations before next deploy.

trevor: Can you paste the profiler snapshot? I suspect kernel selection is amplifying workspace usage for long-context requests — some fused kernels reserve big scratch buffers.

maya: Paste from the lightweight profiler:
```
alloc_free_count: 120k
largest_free_block: 48MB
total_free: 1.1GB
total_allocated: 9.6GB
fragmentation_est: 62%
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.72
oom_events: 7 (last 6h)
most_common_fallback: fallback_alloc_small
```
Notably, when requests hit the larger fused attention path we see transient spikes that force many tiny allocations.

sanjeev: That fragmentation #% is the smoking gun. Two levers: allocator bin granularity + buffer pooling. If bins are too coarse we fragment; if they're too fine we increase metadata. Also buffer reuse (retaining freed buffers in a per-device pool) cuts churn.

luis: Watch the cache tradeoff — reducing shard_count or lowering TTL reduces memory but will drop hit rate and increase model compute. Measured on a sample: shard_count=32 -> hit=0.72, shard_count=16 -> hit=0.61, mem drop ~35%. So must measure cost of extra tokens vs saved GPU memory.

perf-bot: automated-note: current rolling averages: kv_cache_hit_rate=0.72, avg_prefix_tokens=120, p95_latency_change=+12% (since 03:00 UTC), recent OOMs=7.

trevor: Another angle: kernel selection heuristics. The runtime picks a fused-kernel when seq_len>256 which unfortunately needs a larger workspace. If we bias to choose the non-fused path for long seqs we trade some kernel perf for smaller peak memory. Could be a quick emergency knob.

maya: Good idea. I can flip the kernel policy on a canary pool. Also want to try: 1) enable buffer_reuse=true, 2) reduce shard_count to 24, 3) lower per-shard prealloc from 64MB -> 32MB, 4) bump TTL slightly so we don't thrash evictions.

sanjeev: Sketch of allocator changes that helped in labs:
- reduce bin_base from 64k -> 16k for small allocations
- enable per-thread caching for bins to avoid global lock contention
- add retained_buffer_pool with cap 1GB per-GPU (LRU)
- coalesce adjacent free blocks eagerly on free()

Command to try on canary:
```
redwoodctl runtime set-config \
  --pool alpha \
  --allocator bin_base=16384,per_thread_cache=true,retain_pool=1GB \
  --cache shard_count=24,ttl_seconds=1200,prealloc_per_shard=32MB \
  --kernel_policy prefer_nonfused_for_seq_gt=256
```

luis: For observability, capture these metrics per-run: cache_hit_by_shard, avg_evictions_per_min, workspace_peak_by_model, kernel_choice_counts. Also record token-cost delta so we can estimate real cost of hit-rate changes.

trevor: Also adjust batching heuristics if we shrink workspace. For example, lower max_batch_size for token-aware batching when expected seqs>512. Rough heuristic: ensure max_tokens_per_batch * (workspace_per_token) < workspace_limit.

maya: I'll run a matrix of experiments. Plan: run three canaries over 24h each:
- A: buffer_reuse=on, shard=24, ttl=1200, workspace=1.2GB, kernel_policy=nonfused-trigger
- B: buffer_reuse=on, shard=16, ttl=1200, workspace=0.9GB, kernel_policy=keep
- C: buffer_reuse=off, shard=32, ttl=600, workspace=1.2GB, kernel_policy=nonfused-trigger
Will attach benchmarking harness for request mix.

sanjeev: Also add a synthetic workload that stresses many small allocations to validate fragmentation improvements. Script: `python perf/run_cache_sweep.py --matrix shard_count=8,16,24,32 --ttl=600,1200 --workspace=0.8,1.2 --buffer_reuse=on,off`

luis: Quick note: when we lowered shard_count in staging we saw a 0.08 drop in hit rate but latency p95 went up ~8% and token-cost increased ~11%. Keep that in mind when comparing memory saved vs $$$.

maya: Understood. I'll push the canaries and collect the metrics @sanjeev @trevor. Goal: eliminate OOMs and keep token-cost delta <5% if possible.

trevor: If canary is green, we can roll allocator changes to the rest with a slow ramp. Also add a runtime flag to toggle kernel_policy per-model — some models benefit from fused kernels more.

sanjeev: I'll prepare the allocator patch and unit tests (coalescing + pool cap) and post a PR.

luis: Thanks — ping me when you have the metrics dump, I'll run cost analysis. :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks team — starting runs now, will update thread with csv + dashboards. :rocket:
